players.note: Rookie Kaelon Black leading the 49ers' backfield in carries obviously isn't what fantasy managers who spent a first-round pick on CMC wanted to see. But the veteran back was reportedly dealing with cramps; he still racked up his customary elite number of targets (eight). And, although his volume was lower, McCaffrey was actually more efficient on the ground and showed more juice in Week 1 than he did in 2025. Don't overreact to Black's usage — hold CMC and expect elite RB1 production to come.

Saquon averaged a 50% route participation rate in 2025, with a season-low mark of 27%. On Sunday, he tied that low, running nine routes while Will Shipley ran seven. Meanwhile, Barkley failed to find any room to run behind a Philadelphia offensive line that is a far cry from the top-tier unit that helped him dominate in 2024. Saquon's ADP this offseason was a bet on a bounce-back; one week in, that bounce-back doesn't look likely. If you can still cash in on his name brand for legit RB1 value, I'd do it.

The Raiders won't get to play the Dolphins every week. But Ashton Jeanty's usage in Week 1 was excellent, including six targets for an elite 20% target share. Las Vegas' offense also looked competent overall, a huge improvement from last year. With the preseason prayer circle firmly in the rearview mirror, Jeanty is a locked-in RB1 and a steal for anyone who got him at a discount thanks to his ankle injury.

The Saints signed Etienne to a big contract this offseason, presumably to be a workhorse in Kellen Moore's offense. With Alvin Kamara sidelined for Week 1, the veteran should have dominated New Orleans' backfield. Instead, he found himself in an ugly timeshare. Kendre Miller tied Etienne in carries (nine), and UDFA CJ Donaldson served as the team's third-down back. Etienne's final fantasy numbers don't look too bad thanks to a whopping seven receptions, but this isn't good.

After an offseason of worrying about Bucky Irving's role, things were great for the third-year back on Sunday. Kenneth Gainwell did see the team's only two short-yardage carries, but Irving took the lone tote within the 10-yard line (Sean Tucker was sidelined by injury, but reports indicate he isn't headed for much of a role even when healthy). More importantly, Irving racked up a whopping seven targets on a 58% route participation rate. Gainwell, whose receiving ability may have been overrated thanks to playing with Aaron Rodgers last season, saw just one target on a 33% route rate. Especially given Irving also passed the eye test with the juice he showed as a rookie, he's looking set to outperform his draft cost for the rest of the season.

Although he wasn't on the final injury report, Brooks dealt with a groin injury in the lead-up to the Panthers' season-opener. Especially given his injury history, it's not that surprising that he then proceeded to play just 13 snaps against the Bears. But the former second-round pick still managed to flash in his limited role, with a 48-yard reception down the sideline showing off the upside that tempted fantasy managers this offseason. Brooks might not be the Panthers' RB1 any time soon (or ever), but he's absolutely worth holding at least a few weeks longer.

MarShawn Lloyd played his second career NFL game on Sunday; it didn't go well. The 2024 third-rounder was outsnapped by Chris Brooks (37 to 30), who also led the backfield in routes (10 to seven). However, Lloyd did lead the backfield with 13 carries (Brooks saw seven). Former Steeler Kaleb Jonson did not play a snap. Green Bay's rushing offense should bounce back when not facing Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense. If there's upside to be found here while Josh Jacobs remains sidelined, it's Lloyd. Don't give up on him just yet.

This is a sell-high so obvious it might be impossible to actually execute. But it's worth a try, as Week 1 will almost certainly be Chuba Hubbard's best fantasy game of the season. Jonathon Brooks played just 13 snaps on Sunday, but he will likely only get more involved as long as he stays healthy. And even with Brooks mostly a non-factor, Hubbard's actual usage — 10 carries and three targets — was nothing special.

Another player whose Week 1 role failed to live up to offseason hype, Gainwell saw just one target on a 33% route participation rate against the Bengals. Combined with just five carries, his role won't provide standalone value. If you can still sell him based on a draft-day cost that assumed some chance of that standalone value hitting, do it.

The Bears ran absolutely wild in Week 1, and Kyle Monangai was a huge part of it. The second-year back racked up nearly 20 half-PPR points, largely thanks to a massive 61-yard touchdown run. However, Monangai's role wasn't actually all that encouraging: He saw just a 36% RB rush share, with 10 carries to D'Andre Swift's 18 (Swift also saw all three of the team's goal-line attempts). Monangai did outpace his veteran counterpart in targets (two) and route rate (40%), but it's hard to imagine him ever being a consistently large part of this loaded Chicago passing offense. Unless he keeps ripping off huge runs and the Bears keep scoring 50 points a game, Monangai is likely to be an inconsistent, frustrating option in redraft leagues. If you can cash in on the big week and general Bears hype to trade him for weekly starter value, I'd do it.

The third-round rookie led the 49ers' backfield with 14 carries in their shocking upset down under on Thursday, and he looked good doing it. It is worth noting that Christian McCaffrey was reportedly dealing with cramps during the contest — this isn't going to be a true timeshare any time soon. But Black's performance establishes him as at the very least one of the league's most valuable handcuffs, with potential to carve out standalone value a la Blake Corum. He should be rostered in every league.

Obviously, Kenneth Walker III was the story of the Chiefs' Monday night win over the Broncos. But he wasn't the only Kansas City RB to flash, as fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson made the most of his eight carries and two targets. Especially with the Chiefs' offense looking healthier— and more run-heavy — than in recent years, Johnson is a must-add as a top-tier handcuff.
